slides.heading: Palindrome Check
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Easy · Strings
slides.narration: Let's solve Palindrome Check, an easy strings problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Does the string read the same forwards and backwards?
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Does the string read the same forwards and backwards?

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Compare characters from both ends moving inward; any mismatch means it isn't a palindrome.
slides.narration: Compare characters from both ends moving inward; any mismatch means it isn't a palindrome.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Reverse the string and compare → O(n) time, O(n) space
Naive concatenation in a loop → O(n²)
Two pointers → O(n) time, O(1) space
slides.narration: Reversing and comparing works but needs extra space, and building the reverse with repeated concatenation is quadratic. Two pointers from both ends need no extra space.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Left pointer at the start, right at the end
slides.narration: Step by step. First, left pointer at the start, right at the end. Second, compare and move inward. Third, stop when they meet.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: 'a' = 'a' → move inward
slides.narration: Left a matches right a, so both pointers move inward.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: 'b' = 'b' → move inward
slides.narration: Left b matches right b, so both pointers move inward.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: 'c' = 'c' → move inward
slides.narration: Left c matches right c, so both pointers move inward.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Pointers met → palindrome
slides.narration: The pointers meet in the middle with no mismatch, so it's a palindrome.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Left starts at zero and right at the end. While left is less than right, mismatching characters return false; otherwise both move inward. Return true.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Empty and single-character strings are palindromes. Clarify whether to ignore case and punctuation.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: valid palindrome with one deletion
slides.narration: A common follow-up allows deleting one character, or asks for the longest palindromic substring.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Compare characters from both ends moving inward; any mismatch means it isn't a palindrome.
slides.narration: To recap Palindrome Check: Compare characters from both ends moving inward; any mismatch means it isn't a palindrome. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
